questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.topic: What makes two windings couple
questions.learningObjective: Identify the condition for magnetic coupling between two windings
questions.stem: Two coils on separate cores show no induced voltage; what physical link is missing between them?

options.text: A common iron core carrying flux through both coils
A direct electrical connection between terminals
A shared magnetic flux path linking both windings
An identical number of turns in each coil

questions.explanation: Coupling requires flux from one winding to pass through the other. Turn counts and electric links do not create magnetic coupling.
questions.hint: Think about what must physically link the coils.

questions.explanation: Magnetomotive force equals turns times current. 200 times 3 gives 600 ampere-turns.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.topic: Why an air gap dominates a magnetic circuit
questions.learningObjective: Explain why a small air gap dominates reluctance
questions.stem: In a gapped core the air gap is tiny yet its reluctance is huge; why?

options.text: The gap length exceeds the iron path
Flux leaks only through the gap
Air has far lower permeability than iron

questions.explanation: Reluctance scales inversely with permeability. Air's permeability is thousands of times lower than iron's.
questions.hint: Compare permeabilities of air and iron.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.topic: Magnetomotive force across an air gap
questions.learningObjective: Compute mmf drop across an air gap

stimulus.body: A gapped core has gap length 1 mm, area 2 cm^2, flux 1 mWb. Iron reluctance is negligible. Relative permeability of air is 1.

questions.stem: Using the table data, what mmf is required across the air gap?

options.misconception: slips a decimal in area conversion
multiplies by ten in unit conversion

questions.explanation: Gap reluctance = g/(mu0*A) = 0.001/(4pi*1e-7*2e-4) = ~3.98e6. Times 1e-3 Wb = 398 A-turns.
questions.hint: Compute gap reluctance then multiply by flux.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.topic: Effective permeability of a gapped core
questions.learningObjective: Compute effective relative permeability of a gapped core
questions.stem: Core relative permeability 2000, gap fraction 0.001 of total path; estimate effective relative permeability.
questions.explanation: Effective mu_r approximates 1/(gap fraction + 1/mu_r) = 1/(0.001+0.0005) = 667; using simple form gives about 500 for these values.
